clause: Optional external REST/webhook adapter over the command contract [STU-AUT-021,STU-AUT-023]

scope.summary: Implement the OPTIONAL hosted REST/webhook adapter as a posture-correct layer over the command contract for external/cross-process/cloud callers: never required for automation, never the source of authority, never a second command model. REST authentication maps to kernel capability/consent gates (scopes ARE capability names); its event/webhook taxonomy maps to studio.* EventLedger triggers (files/nodes/images/comments/versions/components/variables endpoints + event webhook catalog). Its absence MUST NOT disable any operator/plugin/model automation capability.
expected_tests: live: REST call resolves to a command with capability-mapped auth scope
test: webhook fires on a studio.* EventLedger trigger
negative: disabling REST adapter leaves all local automation working

spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: [STU-AUT-021] Studio's canonical automation entry is **local-first**: the typed command contract exposed as MCP tools (auto-generated from the command `inputSchema`s per [STU-AUT-002]) is the primary programmatic surface, and it is the *same* surface the model lanes drive per 14.16 — Studio exposes its command contract over MCP natively rather than shipping a separate integration server. A hosted REST/webhook surface is an OPTIONAL adapter over the command contract for external, cross-process, or cloud callers; it is never required for automation, never the source of authority, and never a second command model. When present, the REST adapter's authentication maps to the kernel capability/consent gates ([STU-AUT-018]); its scopes are capability names, and its event/webhook taxonomy maps to `studio.*` EventLedger triggers.

[STU-AUT-023] Studio's local automation MUST NOT depend on any vendor account, hosted marketplace, hosted MCP endpoint, or subscription service at runtime ([STU-OVR-002]). External/hosted adapters are opt-in conveniences layered over the local-first command contract, and their absence MUST NOT disable any operator-, plugin-, or model-facing automation capability.

[STU-AUT-018] Plugins MUST run under the kernel capability/consent gate system and MUST NEVER run unsandboxed. A plugin's manifest-declared capabilities are inert until consent-granted; the granted set gates every command the plugin can resolve ([STU-AUT-005]). Plugin execution is sandboxed (process-tier by default, as with model edits per [STU-ARC-005]); a plugin has no ambient filesystem, network, or authority access beyond its consent-granted capabilities. Document mutations authored by a plugin carry a `KernelActor` plugin identity in their receipts and pass the sandbox → validation → `PromotionGate` lifecycle. Plugin UI runs in an isolated surface with no direct access to the native shell's internals; it communicates with the sandboxed plugin logic through a typed message channel.

implementation_notes.naming: Vendor product names are provenance only. Studio ships Handshake-native names per [STU-SECTION-003].
implementation_notes.database: SurrealDB with the EventLedger is the only durable authority. SQLite, libSQL, Turso and PostgreSQL are forbidden, including in tests and dev caches.
implementation_notes.engine_split: GPU, WGSL and compute live in the studio-engine crate behind its traits. handshake_core must never gain a GPU dependency.
implementation_notes.routing: Navigation extends the existing address and bus seams. No new router.
implementation_notes.worktree: Code paths resolve against the WP-KERNEL-012 worktree, never main.

validator_focus: Confirm every acceptance row traces to a sentence in the cited spec clause carried in implementation_notes. A row with no spec basis is a fabrication.
Reject any row still carrying proof_target_status REQUIRED: it has no proof of its own.
Reject scaffold-only proof: at least one proof command must drive the executable runtime rather than a fixture the implementer authored.
Where the contract touches numeric parameters, confirm hard and soft bounds are stored as separate values and an unknown bound is stored as unknown, never mirrored.

resource_privacy_obligation.rule: Resources this contract reads, derives, caches or exports stay inside the authenticated operator's scope. No cross-identity read path may be introduced.
